alignments.note: Entreaty interjection אָנָּה takes the complete English entreaty formula under rule 30, headed on 'beseech'. Cognate accusative repeating the finite verb's own lexeme, which the ASV renders once in 'wept'; rule 22's first sentence marks the unrendered occurrence unrepresented rather than folding it into the rendered one. The competing reading fuses בְּכִי with גָדוֹל into 'sore' under rule 30, but that rule absorbs a morpheme only where the shared word carries its sense, and 'sore' says greatly and not weeping.

Adjective rendered by the adverb 'sore', which is what the ASV spends on the magnitude; where מְאֹד is also written the ASV writes 'very sore', with 'very' on מְאֹד and 'sore' still answering to גָדוֹל.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment fused בְּכִי גָדוֹל into a single 'sore' unit. Rule 30 fuses only where the one English word carries the sense of every morpheme placed in it, and 'sore' writes גָדוֹל's magnitude while the weeping is already written by 'wept' on the finite verb. בְּכִי is therefore the unrendered occurrence of a repeated element under rule 22's first sentence, and גָדוֹל takes 'sore' on its own. The unit count moves from 26 to 27.

Two particles of entreaty stand in the clause and the ASV writes two entreaty renderings ('now' and 'I beseech thee'); each particle takes one, and the competing pairing is named in the אָנָּה unit's note.
בְּעֵינֶיךָ is split three ways because the ASV writes a word for each morpheme, so rule 6's fused reading of בְּעֵינֵי does not reach it.
